key_insight: PI-RADS-compliant prostate MRI can be performed at 0.55T with diagnostic image quality and lesion detection that is close to 3T at the patient level.
clinical_relevance: Low-field prostate MRI could expand access to prostate imaging where higher-field scanners are limited, while keeping scan times clinically practical.
method: 15 healthy male volunteers and 22 patients with suspected prostate cancer underwent bi-parametric prostate MRI at 0.55T.
Protocol used tri-planar T2-weighted imaging and axial DWI aligned with PI-RADS guidance, plus deep learning reconstruction to boost image quality.
Image quality, SNR/CNR, and lesion detection were compared with 3T as the reference in patients.
evidence_signal: At 0.55T, 21/22 patients and all controls reached at least acceptable diagnostic quality, and patient-level lesion detection sensitivity was 91% for both readers versus 3T reference.
watch_item: This is a small single-study feasibility evaluation, so broader validation is needed before assuming equivalent performance across different patient populations and clinical settings.
paper_title: Feasibility of PI-RADS Compliant Prostate MRI at 0.55T
